Etymology

guess

/ɡɛs/  ·  verb & noun  ·  14th century

"to form an opinion … from little or no evidence"

Middle English  gessen
  ← Old Danish  getse, gitse · probably Scandinavian
    ← Proto-Germanic  *gitisōną "to guess"
      ← Proto-Germanic  *getaną "to get"

A guess is an attempt to get it.

What's under the hood
  • word2vec · Google, 2013

  • Every word → 300 numbers

A map with 300 directions

A city = 2 numbers

A word = 300 numbers

tree = [0.484, 0.123, −0.157, 0.035, −0.220, …]

No one decided what the directions mean. The model did.

Similarity = the angle

Same direction → high score

Right angle → zero

"You shall know a word
by the company it keeps."

J.R. Firth, linguist, 1957

The model measures how words are used,
not what they mean.

Why opposites score high

"The water was too ____."

Opposites keep the same company.

good · bad 71.9    up · down 64.0    love · hate 60.0

Why synonyms score low

  • One point per word. bank · river 21.5   bank · money 26.1
  • It read 2013 news. python · snake 66.1   python · java 12.5
  • Usage beats meaning. closest to "guess": suppose, think, yeah
  • Rare words are fuzzy. mercury · quicksilver 14.7

To a model,
a word is a point.

Words are just how it talks to us.

Modern LLMs: thousands of dimensions, and the point moves with context.

Why does it drift?

  • Training rewards the right answer
  • Nothing rewards readable reasoning
  • A language with no listener drifts

The real risk isn't new spellings. It's new meanings.

What we'd lose

  • Early warning. Catch "let's hack" before it happens.
  • Explanations. Why was the loan declined?
  • Debugging. Where did the agent go wrong?
  • Oversight between agents. What are they telling each other?
  • All that's left: judging outcomes.
Exhibit D

Thinking
in Bets

Annie Duke, 2018

search space: every possible future · uncertain

Life is poker,
not chess

Chess

Every piece visible. No dice.

Lose → you made a mistake.

Poker

Hidden cards. Shuffled deck.

Lose → maybe you made a mistake.

"If we aren't wrong just because things didn't work out, then we aren't right just because things turned out well."

Annie Duke, Thinking in Bets

Good decision?

Rate the decision · Round 1

It's 2000. You run the biggest video rental chain on Earth.

  • Thousands of stores. Very profitable.
  • A DVD-by-mail startup offers to sell to you for $50M.
  • It's losing ~$50M a year. It carries debt.
  • The dot-com bubble looks ready to burst.
  • You could copy their model yourself.

Buy or pass?

Closer to home

The spot market, in 10 seconds

The last generator needed sets the price for everyone.

example from AEMC, "How the spot market works" fact sheet (2017)

Rate the decision

2021: skip the hedge?

A small energy retailer skips expensive hedge contracts.

Buys straight from the spot market. Prices have been low for years. Undercuts the big players.

Good decision?

June 2022: AEMO suspends the spot market. First time ever.

~10 small retailers fail within two years.

Meanwhile, the hedgers spent years looking like they'd overpaid.

SBS News (15 Jun 2022); Clayton Utz (2022); RenewEconomy (2023)

Resulting a model

Judging an AI by whether its answer was right,
not by how it got there.

  • "The demo went well. Ship it." One hand of poker.
  • "+2% on the benchmark." One run, or real?
  • "The agent finished the task." But how?

Outcome

Process

Turned off the security team's alerts.

Removed its own monitoring.
Then said it hadn't.

Now imagine that reasoning

Hot take

AI reasoning will
disappear from view.

Hot take

We'll be left
judging outcomes.

Hot take

Outcomes can't tell
bad choices from bad luck.

Every guess
is a bet.

Judge the bet, not the result.

While we still can.
